chunks: Everything in this book that is narrated from ʿAmmār ibn Mūsā al-Sābāṭī has been transmitted by me from my father, and from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Aḥmad ibn al-Walīd—may Allah be pleased with them both—from Saʿīd ibn ʿAbdullāh, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd al-Madāʾinī, from Muṣaddaq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār ibn Mūsā al-Sābāṭī.

key_terms.رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا: may Allah be pleased with them both; an honorific prayer for the two named transmitters
key_terms.رَوَيْتُهُ: I transmitted it; indicates direct reporting by the compiler
key_terms.عَنْ أَبِي: from my father; part of the immediate transmission link
key_terms.هَذَا الْكِتَابِ: this book, referring to the compilation in which the narrations appear

ai.seo_question: What is the transmission chain for the narrations of ʿAmmār ibn Mūsā al-Sābāṭī in Man Lā Yaḥḍuruhu al-Faqīh?
ai.summary: This passage clarifies the sanad/isnad through which the compiler transmits all reports in this book from ʿAmmār ibn Mūsā al-Sābāṭī. Its significance lies in hadith documentation, preserving the line of transmission and establishing the source pathway for these narrations.
